problems.source_says: Table 2 defines text elaboration as a word count. The paper identifies neither a creativity scoring model nor an LLM judge for this outcome, and does not state whether the words were counted automatically. Gemini OCR is described for the separate semantic analysis. The codebook defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity, so the form's acknowledged closest-code substitution is unsupported; the measure code should remain null pending an explicit codebook convention for word counts.

problems.source_says: The reported F statistic, p value, Wilks lambda and partial eta squared test the AI-usage-by-condition-order interaction using both assisted and unaided scores. They do not test the stated comparison of Group B's unaided Task 2 flexibility with Group A's unaided Task 1 flexibility. The printed means and ANOVA numbers are transcribed correctly, and the form acknowledges that no direct test of this pair is reported, but its statistics_available still marks test_statistic for that contrast. Keep the arm descriptives under after_ai and separate the omnibus interaction from that contrast's inferential statistics.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: the submitted ideas, descriptions and drawings receive output-based counts or scores; the semantic analyses embed those descriptions. These are not self-reported creativity outcomes.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.3; p. 7, Table 2 and Section 3.3.2.

confirmed.statement: The AI-assisted arm had ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) available while producing its outputs; unaided participants could not use computers, electronic devices or external resources. The immediate AI-availability coding for S1-O1 through S1-O11 is supported for the assisted arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.1; p. 4, two-hour session description.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 measures participant fluency as the number of ideas; S1-O2 measures participant flexibility as the number of LV2 categories explored. category_count and with_ai fit both.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 2; pp. 8-9, Tables 4-5 and their participant-count notes; codebook Sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 measures rarity through counts of Unique Ideas and Unique Solutions, supporting novelty/category_count. S1-O4 counts Existing Solutions, with lower counts meaning greater novelty; its reversed direction is appropriate. Both use participant observations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.2.2; p. 7, Table 2; pp. 8-9, Tables 4-5; codebook Section 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 is elaboration of produced descriptions, analyzed at participant level. S1-O6 uses three binary drawing features for image elaboration and also has participant-level statistics; the paper does not identify the drawing scorer.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 2; pp. 8-9, Tables 4-5; pp. 5-6, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.3.

confirmed.statement: Every mean, SD, z, U, p and r recorded for S1-O1 through S1-O6 matches the corresponding Table 4 or Table 5 cell, including the printed signs and significance markers.

The stated Methods for S1-O7 average pairwise divergence within each participant's own ideas, supporting flexibility, embedding_similarity, with_ai and the stated participant unit. The Results instead describe centroid divergence and print t(364); the form already flags both source inconsistencies.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2; p. 10, Section 4.3; p. 11, Fig. 3(b); codebook Section 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O8 computes each idea's embedding distance to its condition centroid across participants: diversity/across_people, embedding_similarity and output are supported. The paper gives 368 assisted and 360 unaided ideas.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2; p. 10, Section 4.3; codebook Sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: All semantic-divergence means, SDs, t statistics, printed degrees of freedom, p values, d values and confidence limits in S1-O7 and S1-O8 match the PDF. Printed means and Fig. 3 place assisted divergence higher, while the prose says lower; the form explicitly records that contradiction.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3; p. 11, Fig. 3(a)-(b); p. 13, Section 5.3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O9 uses each condition's whole idea pool for category-based diversity, supporting diversity/across_people and set. Its category counts, Shannon and Simpson indices and printed differences match Tables 6-7.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2; p. 9, Table 6; p. 10, Table 7 and preceding text.

confirmed.statement: S1-O10 compares the category size assigned to each idea, supporting an output-level thematic-diversity analysis. Its N, means, SDs, U, z and p match the source; the category level is unspecified, as the form states.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2; p. 10, Section 4.3, category-size paragraph.

confirmed.statement: The paper treats condition differences in unique-contribution frequencies as thematic homogenisation, supporting the collective comparison in S1-O11. Its idea-level chi-square tests use N = 728, and all Unique Idea, Unique Solution and Existing Solution counts and test statistics match the source.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, research question 3; pp. 5-6, Section 3.2.2; p. 9, Table 6; p. 10, Section 4.3.

confirmed.statement: S1-O12 through S1-O15 correctly identify Group B's Task 2 output as immediate after_ai work with AI unavailable. Their constructs and participant units follow the corresponding creativity metrics, and all displayed unaided-cell means and SDs match Table 5.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because creativity and diversity are scored on participants' submitted ideas and drawings. Full coding accuracy is refuted by the unsupported automated_score label for word counts and by ANOVA tests assigned to three after_ai contrasts that those tests do not evaluate.
